entry.title: Valve Announces Steam Frame VR Headset Pricing
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source | hacker news

Valve's Steam Frame VR headset will retail for $1,059 for the 256GB model and $1,200 for the 1TB model. The device supports standalone operation via SteamOS or tethered use with a computer. Additional accessories include a $29 standalone power supply and a $59 ergonomic kit.

The pricing is influenced by a computer memory shortage driven by increased demand from AI firms. Unlike competitors like Meta, Valve is not subsidizing hardware costs to drive software sales. Developers can acquire device kits through the Steam Partner dashboard.

entry.title: Laurelyn McWills Discusses Integrating Emotional Connections into Game Systems
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com

Designing game systems to elicit specific player emotions allows developers to address fundamental human needs through core gameplay mechanics. Laurelyn McWills advocates for "experiential core loops" that connect psychological motivations—such as agency, mastery, or social connection—directly to systemic rewards and player interactions.

Using case studies from Full Spectrum Warrior and Free Realms, McWills demonstrates how systemic changes, such as mission-based rescue objectives and social-based leveling, can maintain immersion and reinforce emotional engagement. Her approach moves beyond traditional combat loops to create a tighter connection between player motivation and gameplay mechanics.

entry.title: Valve Announces Steam Frame Standalone VR Headset
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | store.steampowered.com | hacker news

The Steam Frame is a standalone VR headset from Valve, available in 256GB and 1TB configurations. The 256GB model is priced at $1,059, while the 1TB version is $1,299. The hardware includes 16GB of RAM, microSD expansion, and dual 2160 x 2160 LCD displays with refresh rates between 72Hz and 144Hz.

Built around the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor, the headset is designed for both standalone use and PC VR connectivity. Each unit includes a copy of Half-Life: Alyx, and users can purchase additional accessory kits or power supplies to support different operating modes.

entry.title: Polyarc Shuts Down After Nearly 12 Years
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Seattle-based VR studio Polyarc, the developer behind the Moss franchise, has announced its closure after nearly 12 years in operation. The studio confirmed it is winding down active development in a post on LinkedIn.

The shutdown follows significant downsizing in March 2026 due to financing challenges. While official layoff figures have not been released, a reverse recruiting tracker indicates approximately 30 staff members have been let go.

entry.title: KO_OP Confirms 13 Layoffs
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The worker-run indie studio behind *Goodbye Volcano High* and *Young Suns* has laid off 13 employees, including team leads and elected executives. The studio cited a shift in the gaming funding landscape and an inability to secure financing for new projects as the driving factors behind the decision.

The layoffs were made via a democratic process aimed at ensuring the studio's survival. KO_OP announced that profits from *Young Suns* will still be shared with the impacted team members and expressed an intention to rehire staff if the studio secures funding in the coming months.

entry.title: xkcd Fonts Derived from Randall Munroe's Handwriting
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion

Two typefaces based on the handwriting of xkcd creator Randall Munroe are available in this repository. The collection includes `xkcd Script`, a less uniform typeface designed to resemble a natural script, and a more legible, uniform version titled `xkcd`.

The `xkcd` font was originally used in the 2013 webcomic "The Pace of Modern Life." Both fonts are provided in TTF, WOFF, and OTF formats under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 License.

entry.title: Steam Requires Australian Users to Verify Age via Credit Card
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Steam now requires Australian users to verify their age using a valid Australian credit card to access R18+ rated games. This requirement is a response to the Age-Restricted Material App Distribution Services Code, which mandates age verification for mature-rated content and websites in Australia.

The implementation has faced criticism from users who report a lack of alternative verification methods, such as government IDs, passports, or PayPal. This has raised concerns that adults who rely solely on debit cards may be unable to access mature content on the platform.

entry.title: Xbox to Publish Kojima Productions' Physint After PlayStation Exit
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The espionage game Physint will be published by Xbox after PlayStation Studios rescinded its partnership with Kojima Productions. This new agreement also includes expanded collaboration across film and television to reach broader audiences.

Hideo Kojima sought a new partner for three months after receiving notice from PlayStation to cancel the project. Through this expanded partnership, Xbox will also support the studio's upcoming project, OD - Knock.

entry.title: Turnkey Games Founders Discuss Transitioning from AAA to Indie Development
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Former id Software employees Tony Garza and Richard O'Neal founded Turnkey Games to gain creative control and bypass the instability of AAA studio environments. They advocate for a lean, bootstrapped development model that prioritizes core gameplay features and avoids the excessive technical scaling and scope creep typical of large-scale studio productions.

The studio's methodology for the development of their debut title, Apart, emphasizes maintaining momentum through iterative design and "good enough" solutions to manage budgets. While the founders highlight the rewards of direct ownership, they note that indie development requires managing significantly more personal financial, technical, and operational risk.
